options-flow-feed-lab.lean=call-heavy (leaning bullish); tickers=12; contractsOver250k=1957; horizonDays=30; topPrint=IWM 302P $3.7M on 69.8x OI
items.method: Cross-read the market-heatmap breadth percentage against its 60% threshold and against the benchmark's distance from its 52-week high and its moving-average stack, then overlay the option-flow call lean, contract count and the single most-unusual print, and the VIX band, to judge whether an index holding near its high on broad breadth is being confirmed by demand or still carrying a downside hedge at the margin.
items.note: Breadth and premium sit aligned bullishly into this pre-market window, with one hedged tail. The SPY benchmark last printed 769.06, only 1.13% under its 52-week high, in a bull-stacked moving-average regime (50-day distance +2.48%, 200-day +8.82%, 126-day momentum +12.06%), and 64.33% of the 134 market-heatmap constituents are positive on the day — a 4.33-point cushion above the 60% broad-participation threshold, even as a qualified double-top pattern still stands overhead. Premium flow reads call-heavy and leaning bullish across 12 tickers with 1957 contracts clearing the $250k bar inside 30 days, so broad participation and bullish positioning agree rather than diverge. The one dissonant note is that the single most-unusual print is an IWM 302 put at $3.7M on 69.8x its open interest — a small-cap downside hedge sitting against an otherwise bullish tape. VIX 14.97 keeps this in a calm, positive-gamma-adjacent band. So an index pinned near its high on broad breadth with call-led premium is a constructive alignment, and what to watch is whether breadth holds above 60% to keep confirming the premium or the double top caps the advance while that small-cap hedge widens.
items.title: SPY holds about 1% under its 52-week high as daily breadth runs 64.3% above the 60% line and confirms the call-led premium, yet the single most-unusual print is a downside IWM put hedge

inputs: options-structure-lab.regime=negative dealer gamma; flip=769.54; callWall=770; putWall=765; expectedMove=2.77
items.method: Read the options-structure gamma sign with its flip and wall levels against current benchmark spot, size the expected-move band around spot, confirm the dealer scenario and conviction from the gamma playbook, then overlay the intraday session type and VWAP and the VIX band, to judge whether short-gamma dealers are positioned to accelerate a break of the nearest wall or whether the corridor holds.
items.note: Dealer positioning and price sit in a pinched gamma corridor into this window. Signed dealer gamma is negative, and SPY near 769.06 is just under the 769.54 flip, wedged between the 765 put wall and the 770 call wall. The front expected move is plus or minus 2.77, so both walls sit close to the edges of the modelled band, roughly 766.3 to 771.8 around spot. Under negative gamma dealers hedge in the direction of the move, so sustained pressure toward a wall tends to extend rather than mean-revert. The gamma playbook reads range-break-watch with patient conviction, and the prior session was a range day under algo-controlled conditions with VWAP 769.85 just above spot. The flow tape leans call-heavy overall, but the most-unusual single print is a downside IWM 302 put, consistent with hedging into the corridor. This is a coiled structure: while 765 holds and VIX 14.97 stays calm it can stay orderly, but a sustained loss of the 765 put wall in short gamma is what would tip the balance toward downside acceleration, whereas a clean reclaim of the 770 call wall would relieve the corridor to the upside.
items.title: SPY spot near 769.06 rests just below the 769.54 negative-gamma flip inside the 765 put wall and 770 call wall, with a plus-or-minus 2.77 expected move that bounds both walls

items.method: Cross-read the real-assets per-vehicle scores and the 63-day driver block (crypto and industrial XLI versus gold, broad commodities and the gold/silver ratio) against the equity sector rotation and the benchmark regime, to judge whether the real-asset bid is risk-appetite-and-cyclical-led or monetary, and whether it agrees with where equity leadership is rotating.
items.note: The real-asset bid and the equity rotation disagree on risk appetite this window. Within real assets, crypto leads — ETH-USD at 69.5/100 and BTC-USD 62 in uptrends — while broad commodities DBC 55.4 and PDBC 55.3 and industrial copper CPER 57.3 hold firm, and the monetary metals lag: gold GLD reads 48 and mixed while silver SLV 23.8 is weak; IBIT 42.2 and oil USO 38.3 are mixed; 14 vehicles scored on a swing horizon. The driver block corroborates the risk-on, cyclical tilt: the 63-day bitcoin proxy runs +10.52 and the industrial proxy +7.83 against a gold proxy of only +0.57 and a broad-commodity proxy of -2.69, and the gold-versus-silver ratio proxy is +12.12, meaning gold is outpacing silver. Yet the equity sector rotation reads the other way defensively — into XLU (Improving, accel +4.37), out of XLF (Weakening), with XLV (healthcare) Leading. So the real-asset complex leans risk-on through crypto and copper while the equity leadership leans defensive; the tension is whether the crypto-and-cyclical strength persists or converges down to the cautious equity read. VIX 14.97 is calm and the benchmark holds near its high, so this is a rotation-quality divergence rather than a stress signal.
items.title: Real-asset leadership is crypto (ETH-USD 69.5, BTC-USD 62) and industrial copper (CPER 57.3) over monetary gold (GLD 48) and silver (SLV 23.8) while equity sector rotation turns defensive into XLU with XLV leading
